title: Revisiting the logical independence
summary: It has been widely acknowledged that probabilistic independence and logical independence cannot be coherently reconciled. By bridging these two notions, this paper addresses three long-standing problems that have puzzled the field of probability theory: Should probability be defined prior to independence, or independence prior to probability? How ought independence to be formulated for signed measures and families of probability measures?
